- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.67) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., <0.30 or 0.00) — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Lag in correction: model often delays downward adjustments after negative sentiment, especially if recent prices are high.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, failing to smoothly revert to historical mean in 30-day horizon.
- Sentiment-weighted smoothing: when sentiment is consistently low or volatile, reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence.
- Avoid “peak-predict” traps: if last 3–5 days show sharp upward movement, model tends to overforecast next period — apply downward bias of 2–5% for 2–3 periods.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish — cap early forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high.
